<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **91** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **14** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/hook-bodies.mdx`  _(via body.source (literal, a string literal in undeclaredActionRefusalCodeAtSave; a string literal in undeclaredActionRefusalReasonAtSave))_
- `content/docs/deployment/troubleshooting.mdx`  _(via ActionSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/frontend/architecture-overview.mdx`  _(via ActionSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/frontend/troubleshooting.mdx`  _(via ActionSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/actions.mdx`  _(via ActionRefusal (symbol, a top-level type), ActionSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via ActionSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via ActionSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via bindAppArtifactHandlers (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/index.mdx`  _(via ActionSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via ActionSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via ActionSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via ActionSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **14** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `objectName (symbol, 59 pages)`
- **13** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **178** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c513d62acdd342745bbfe29786ba4b644cd934fc` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `55d9cc8c7be4450b02c5593cafdadb7896b5c5c1` — the merge of head `0169fc10be77711968755536013f9d09d48868a4` into base `c513d62acdd342745bbfe29786ba4b644cd934fc`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 55d9cc8c7be4450b02c5593cafdadb7896b5c5c1 && git checkout 55d9cc8c7be4450b02c5593cafdadb7896b5c5c1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c513d62acdd342745bbfe29786ba4b644cd934fc 0169fc10be77711968755536013f9d09d48868a4 && git checkout -B drift-repro c513d62acdd342745bbfe29786ba4b644cd934fc && git merge --no-ff 0169fc10be77711968755536013f9d09d48868a4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c513d62acdd342745bbfe29786ba4b644cd934fc
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c513d62acdd342745bbfe29786ba4b644cd934fc` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**L1 first review · ACCEPT** · head `ff1ba6635716487e6d8b5a54f4834c9dce7bbc4a` (final head 6947051003) · card #34273 · read 2026-11-17T11:45Z

### Checklist (read on GitHub at this head, not from the report)

- **Shape:**
  - Draft PR against `main`, `mergeable_state: clean`.
  - The only closing-keyword hit is `Fixes #34273`.
  - The footer is in AGENTS.md's form.
  - The claim (6931334915, 2026-11-16) predates the wind-down.
- **Declarations:**
  - `Clause-②: yes (widening)` holds, read from the diff:
    - `ActionSchema.refusals` is a new optional key.
    - The translation node gains `refusals`.
    - The save-time refusals (a catalogue on an action with no `js` body; a literal undeclared code or reason) apply only to an action that declares `refusals`, with CONTROLs for "no catalogue".
    - The runtime: `resolveActionRefusal` returns `err` unchanged when `catalogueOf(action)` is empty, so an action without `refusals` answers as before (CONTROL pinned). A crash and a host-relayed error pass through `resolveSandboxedRefusal` untouched.
  - `Metadata-protocol: added` is right: a new key.
  - `Skills-docs: follow-up` is acceptable for an `added` kind. The follow-up is named: `objectstack-i18n` and the action `refusals`.
- **Shared factory:** `declared-entry.zod.ts` builds `HookRefusalSchema`, `ActionRefusalSchema` and `HookTextSchema` from one core. The body claims the published hook schemas are byte-identical, and the generated set agrees: no `json-schema` or reference page for hooks moves, and `check:generated` and CI are green.
- **Wiring:** `body-runner.ts` hands every action-body throw to `resolveActionRefusal` before logging. Both default action-runner bindings (`app-plugin.ts`, `app-artifact-handlers.ts`) now pass the `i18n` reader.
- **Tests:** 16 runtime cases over the real `actionBodyRunnerFactory` + QuickJS and the real `/actions` door, including 409 + zh-CN `userMessage` and its CONTROL. There are 29 spec cases, plus lint +12/+4/+3. Each of the 5 forced test changes is named with its reason. The ablation turned 12 of 16 red; the 4 that stayed green are the pass-through CONTROLs.
- **Gates at this head:**
  - Check-runs on `ff1ba663…`: 74 runs, all completed: 63 `success`, 11 `skipped`, 0 failed.
  - `git merge-tree --write-tree` against today's `origin/main` is clean.
  - `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 34719`, read here: **GOVERNED**, 2 of 51 paths. The two are `skills/objectstack-data|ui/references/_index.md`, and the generated-surface exception did not lift them. Size is 2353 lines.

### Before landing (no head move)

- **Card surface amendment.** The claim's surface is stop-on-breach. These paths lie outside it, and the card has no amendment for them:
  - `packages/spec/src/data/declared-entry.zod.ts` (new);
  - `ui/packages/core/src/actions/actionKeys.ts`, which adds `refusals` to the key roster so the console does not report it unknown;
  - `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts` and `authored-site-expression.test.ts`;
  - `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.meta-types-degenerate-derivation.test.ts`;
  - `docs/audits/2026-07-unknown-key-strictness-ledger.*`;
  - the two generator-owned `skills/*/references/_index.md` lines.

  The dev report lists them, and each looks forced, either by the factory or by a gate. Please post one claim amendment on #34273 that names them with that reason.

### Residuals (no change asked)

- `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` grows by 21 sites for `ActionRefusal` (header 270 / 1135). It is generated and gate-accepted, and recorded here for the contract tier.
- The Studio action form gets no `refusals` row (ledgered omission), and the skills teaching is a follow-up.

### Owed after this

- **L2: owed, `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`.** The faces are non-test `packages/spec/src`, `Clause-②: yes` with `Metadata-protocol: added`, and governed `skills/**`.
- **Landing tier: governed (`skills/**`) and the spec face, Tier H.** It stays a draft until `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` approve.

l2-review#4 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmP44onN8RMzsPMqjRq

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ff1ba6635716487e6d8b5a54f4834c9dce7bbc4a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/declared-entry.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/hook-refusal-codes.ts, packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts, packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts, skills/objectstack-data/references/_index.md, skills/objectstack-ui/references/_index.md + packages/runtime/src/sandbox/hook-refusal-catalogue.ts, packages/runtime/src/sandbox/body-runner.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-hook-refusal-templates.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts, packages/lint/src/i18n-walk.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-translation-references.ts, ui/packages/core/src/actions/actionKeys.ts
Security-touching: yes
Reason for the line above: the published schema text and example added in `packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts` teach an action body answering an unauthenticated caller with a declared 401 (`SIGN_IN_REQUIRED`, the card's own second scenario), and the runtime hunks change what a caller is shown of a body's throw (declared sentence on `userMessage`, the body's own text withheld, an undeclared throw answered as a 500 fault). The dev report's `security_findings` field reads `withheld`, so its content was not available to this review. The two skills hunks themselves are generator pointer rows and teach no security behaviour; the `yes` is meant, on the strength of the spec and runtime hunks, so the PR should not land on the low-risk skills arm.

Inputs read: card #34273 body and its four comments (triage 6906711719, ruling 6919184064, claim 6931334915, dev report 6944561600); PR #34719 body, its five comments (lane final note 6947051003 included), the 51-file list and the net diff from merge-base `6dd57163295f` to the head; the check-runs on the head.

### ① Derived judgments

Check-runs on the head: 74 runs, every one `success` or `skipped`, none failed, none pending. Skipped are the opt-in or path-filtered lanes (Temporal Conformance, Dogfood Verify CLI, UI Published Artifacts, queue verdicts, upgrade harness, packed-tarball smoke, the schedule gate) and the edit-event reruns of Auto Label and Check PR Size, both green on the push event. Spec property liveness, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Lint and Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core and Test UI are all `success`. The derived gate families are answered by these.

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged:

- `ActionSchema.refusals` (new optional key, record keyed by `HOOK_REFUSAL_CODE_PATTERN`, value `ActionRefusalSchema`): right, a widening. The action object is strict, so the key was refused as unknown before; an action without it parses and runs exactly as before (the new superRefine returns at once when `refusals` is absent).
- `ActionRefusalSchema` / `ActionRefusal` exported from `@objectstack/spec/ui`: right, additive; `api-surface/ui.json`, `authorable-surface/ui.json` (`ui/Action:refusals` plus the four `ui/ActionRefusal:*` keys) and `json-schema.manifest/ui.json` move with it.
- Hook refusal accept-set after the factory refactor: right, unchanged. Read line against line: `declaredRefusalEntrySchema('hook')` reproduces the removed `HookRefusalSchema` literal exactly — `surface`, `history`, the ten aliases, both guidance sentences, `message` (trim, min 1), `status` (int 400..499), `reasons` keyed by `HOOK_REFUSAL_REASON_PATTERN` with the same strict reason object, `params` over `HOOK_REFUSAL_PARAM_PATTERN`, and the superRefine in the same issue order (duplicate param, own message, each reason) with the same slot string `A hook refusal \`message\`` and the same two sentence rules. No narrowing and no widening on the hook side.
- `HookTextSchema` via `declaredTextEntrySchema('hook')`: right, unchanged — same surface, aliases, `locale` guidance, `message` and `params` describes, param-pattern message, slot `A hook text \`message\`` and hole refusal.
- Hook sentences in `hook-refusal-codes.ts`: right, byte-identical. `undeclaredHookRefusalCodeAtSave`, `undeclaredHookRefusalAtRun`, `undeclaredHookRefusalReasonAtSave`, `undeclaredHookRefusalReasonAtRun` and `HOOK_REFUSAL_MESSAGE_HOLE_REFUSED` keep their signatures and, with subject `hook` and article `A hook`, produce the sentences they produced on `main`. Corroborated by the diff carrying no change to the generated hook reference page and no hook row in `dropped-refinements.baseline.json`; `liveness/hook.json` moves only the `params` producer anchor to the factory.
- Hook message keys: right, unchanged — `hookRefusalMessageKey` and `hookTextMessageKey` are untouched; `hooks.HOOK.refusals` in `translation.zod.ts` is rebuilt by `refusalTranslationsSchema('hook')` with the same surface names, aliases and describe text as the removed literal.
- Six new exports on `@objectstack/spec/data` (`ACTION_REFUSAL_MESSAGE_HOLE_REFUSED`, `actionRefusalsWithoutSandboxedBody`, `undeclaredActionRefusalCodeAtSave`, `undeclaredActionRefusalReasonAtSave`, `undeclaredActionRefusalAtRun`, `undeclaredActionRefusalReasonAtRun`) and `actionRefusalMessageKey` on `@objectstack/spec/system`: right, additive, recorded in `api-surface` and `export-origins`.
- Translation bundles: `objects.OBJ._actions.ACT.refusals.CODE.message`, `.reasons.REASON.message`, and the same under `globalActions.ACT`: right, a widening of a strict node (alias `refusal` renamed onto `refusals`). One `actionTranslationSchema` factory serves both addresses, so the two cannot differ.
- `packages/spec/src/data/declared-entry.zod.ts` stays off every barrel: right — neither `declaredRefusalEntrySchema` nor `declaredTextEntrySchema` appears in `api-surface/data.json`.
- `@objectstack/lint`: `actionRefusalTemplateIssues`, `pushActionRefusals`, `checkActionRefusals` judge only an action that carries `refusals` or a bundle that carries a `refusals` key under an action, both unparseable before: right, no previously accepted document is newly refused. The hook pass keeps its `where` string and its currency sentence.
- `@objectstack/runtime`: the action body runner now hands every body throw to `resolveActionRefusal`, which returns the error itself when the action declares no catalogue: right, behaviour-preserving without the key. `resolveHookRefusal` and `resolveInProcessHookRefusal` reach the same sentences, key, status and error shape through `hookOwner`.
- `@object-ui/core` `SPEC_ACTION_KEYS` gains `refusals`: right, it restates the spec's declared keys.
- The dev's claim that `@objectstack/runtime` exports `resolveActionRefusal`: wrong, see S1 in ②.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/34273-action-refusals.md`: `@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/runtime` minor, `@objectstack/lint` minor, `@object-ui/core` patch. The levels match what the diff publishes: a new authorable key and new exports (spec), a new answered behaviour on the public `actionBodyRunnerFactory` and both default bindings (runtime), new passes that only read the new key (lint), one restated key (ui core). Nothing is removed or narrowed, so no major is owed. `Check Changeset` is `success` on the head.

`Clause-②: yes (widening)` is the right arm: every change in ① is an addition, and the hook side is unchanged. `Metadata-protocol: added` is right (`action` serves one more top-level property).

S1 (should-fix) — the `Clause-②:` line, in the PR body and in the changeset body that becomes the published changelog, states that `@objectstack/runtime` exports `resolveActionRefusal`. At the head it does not: `resolveActionRefusal` is exported only by the module `packages/runtime/src/sandbox/hook-refusal-catalogue.ts`; `packages/runtime/src/index.ts` re-exports from `./sandbox/index.js` only the runners, `SandboxError` and the two body-runner factories, `packages/runtime/src/sandbox/index.ts` names no refusal symbol, and the package `exports` map has no subpath that reaches the file. A consumer cannot import the name from the package. Either re-export it from the package barrel (with `ActionRefusalDeclaration`) or reword the line in both places to say the action body runner answers through it internally. The semver level is unaffected.

N1 (nit) — the same line names two of the nine new spec exports; the six `@objectstack/spec/data` sentence exports and the `ActionRefusal` type are published too. The arm and the level do not change.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev `open_questions`, the one entry (contract review at the earlier head `2a25dade9108`, options A send / B hold): answered A by this record, rendered on the final head `ff1ba6635716` named in lane note 6947051003.
- Dev flag, `security_findings: withheld`: not answerable from the inputs. Escalated to the adopting seat: read the withheld field through its own channel before adopting; the `yes` on the security line above stands regardless.
- Dev flag, out-of-scope finding (class b): the Studio action form has no `refusals` row; the reconciliation ledger carries an omit row. Accepted as a follow-up (the `hook.texts` precedent), but the report says `noted, not filed`: the seat files the card before ACCEPT.
- Dev flag, out-of-scope finding (class b) and `Skills-docs: follow-up`: no skill teaches an action's `refusals`; `skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md` lists the hook key only. Judged a fair follow-up, not a gap this PR must close: no skill line at the head states anything the diff makes false (the hook teaching in `skills/objectstack-data/references/data-hooks.md` and the i18n skill still holds, and nothing says an action cannot declare one), the card's Expected section asks for the declaration, the pack key and the localized answer and names no skill, and `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx` and `content/docs/ui/translations.mdx` teach it here. Two things are owed by the seat: the PR-body and changeset line is spelled `follow-up —` where the protocol spelling is `follow-up owed — FILES`, and the owed card is not filed; file it and rewrite the line to `follow-up #N` before ACCEPT.
- Dev deviations (five forced test edits; the two generated skills rows): the test edits are the lane seat's ACCEPT; the skills rows are judged in ④.
- Dev flag, translation address differs from the card face (`actions.ACTION.refusals…` on the card, `objects.OBJ._actions.ACT.refusals…` / `globalActions.ACT.refusals…` in the diff): right, recorded on claim 6931334915; the action node is the address every other action translation is read at, and the top-level `actions` pack key is a refused alias.
- Not covered, as declared: a string `target` with no body (a registered host handler) is not answered against a catalogue. Consistent: `refusals` is refused at save there, so nothing is promised.
- SQL push-down: no finding. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join; the runtime change is an error-mapping step in the action body runner.

### ④ Design judgment
